title: Adverse event following immunization or vaccination in children in Minas Gerais: 2015 to 2020.
ehr_evidence: This is an ecological, descriptive study with a quantitative approach, based on ESAVI notifications registered in the PNI Information System (Sistema de Informações do PNI – SI-PNI).
summary: An ecological, descriptive study of immunization errors among children aged 0 to 9 years in Minas Gerais, Brazil (2015–2020), using ESAVI notifications from the national immunization information system to characterize the frequency and clinical features of events supposedly attributable to vaccination.
key_findings: 3,259 immunization errors were recorded out of 39,903,277 doses administered, equivalent to 0.008% of total doses.
91.86% of immunization errors did not result in adverse events and 8.14% resulted in an adverse event.
56.02% of errors occurred in children under 1 year of age.
The most frequent diagnosis was application outside the recommended age (29.12%).
71.91% of manifestations were local and systemic, with fever being the most common systemic manifestation (40.85%).
The incidence rate of immunization errors without adverse events was 7.50/100,000 doses administered and with adverse events 0.66/100,000 doses.
In 2019 the highest incidence rate of errors without adverse events (16.18/100,000) and with adverse events (1.06/100,000) was observed.
population: Children aged 0 to 9 years in Minas Gerais, Brazil, 2015 to 2020
exposure_domain: Immunization/vaccination errors and adverse events following immunization
limitations: Ecological study design limiting causal inference.
Underreporting of ESAVIs resulting from immunization errors.
Inadequate/incomplete completion of notification records (e.g., 99.69% of errors without adverse events lacked case-evolution information).
Use of secondary data from a public-health surveillance information system.
